properties.natural_language: A block received from a P2P peer must contain a valid parent hash referencing an existing block in the local chain database before header validation begins.

All block header fields (difficulty, gas limit, timestamp, block number) received from an untrusted peer must be individually validated against protocol rules before the block is accepted for transaction processing.
The block's gas limit must be within the allowed adjustment range relative to the parent block's gas limit (parent_gas_limit / 1024 deviation).
After all transactions in a block are processed, the computed state root must exactly match the state root declared in the block header; any mismatch results in block rejection.
The block processing pipeline must be deterministic: given the same parent state and block, every compliant node must arrive at the same post-state root.
A block that fails header validation must never have its transactions executed; the block must transition directly to the BLOCK-INVALID state.
The genesis state must be correctly initialized and considered trusted as the root of all state derivations.
A transaction submitted for execution must have a valid ECDSA signature from which the sender address can be recovered.
The transaction nonce must exactly equal the sender account's current nonce; transactions with mismatched nonces must be rejected.
The sender's account balance must be at least gas_limit * gas_price + value before transaction execution begins.
After transaction execution, unused gas must be refunded to the sender at the original gas price; the refunded amount must equal (gas_limit - gas_used) * gas_price.
The sum of gas deducted from the sender and gas refunded to the sender must equal gas_limit * gas_price; no ETH may be created or destroyed in the gas accounting cycle.
After a trie write operation, the root hash must be recomputed by propagating hash changes from the modified leaf up to the root node.
A trie read for a non-existent key must return the default value (empty/zero); it must never return data from a different key or cause an error.
Proof-of-Work consensus with ethash is assumed active during the Frontier fork; block validation logic depends on this consensus mechanism.
DNS TXT records received from the DNS resolver must have their root record signature verified against the known secp256k1 public key before any node records are imported.
DNS TXT records must not exceed the 512-byte UDP DNS limit; entries exceeding this limit must be rejected as invalid.
The root record's sequence number must be greater than or equal to the previously cached sequence number; a lower sequence number indicates a potential replay/rollback attack and must be rejected.
Branch entry content must match the base32 keccak256 hash of the subdomain; any hash mismatch indicates data corruption or tampering and must be rejected.
No ENR record may be imported into the local node table without first verifying the root signature and content hash integrity of all ancestor nodes in the Merkle tree path.
Clients must use multiple independent DNS discovery sources to mitigate eclipse attacks from any single compromised or malicious DNS list publisher.
The DNS tree traversal must handle recursive resolution without unbounded depth; implementations must enforce a maximum traversal depth to prevent resource exhaustion from maliciously deep trees.
The publisher's secp256k1 public key extracted from the enrtree URL must be validated as a well-formed public key before use in signature verification.
DNS record format must be parseable into one of the known entry types (root, branch, enr, link); unrecognized formats must be rejected.
Even a trusted DNS list publisher can eclipse clients; trust in the publisher does not eliminate the need for source diversification.
The address parameter in a wallet_getOwnedAssets RPC request must be a valid Ethereum address format (20-byte hex with 0x prefix) before any asset query is performed.
The chainId parameter, if provided, must be a valid chain identifier per EIP-155; invalid chain IDs must result in parameter validation failure.
The limit parameter, if provided, must be a positive integer; zero or negative values must be rejected.
Asset type identifiers in the types array must be recognized standards (e.g., ERC20, ERC721); unknown types should return empty results rather than errors.
User consent must be obtained before any asset information is returned to a requesting dApp; the wallet must never return asset data without explicit user approval.
Only assets that the user has explicitly whitelisted for a given dApp may be included in the response; non-whitelisted assets must never be disclosed.
After user approval, the whitelist preferences must be persisted so that subsequent requests from the same dApp can reference the stored permissions.
The requesting dApp's identity must be verified to prevent phishing attacks that harvest user portfolio data by impersonating legitimate applications.
Invalid wallet_getOwnedAssets requests must return standard JSON-RPC error codes (e.g., -32602 for invalid params) rather than silently failing or returning partial data.
GraphQL queries received at the /graphql endpoint must be parsed and validated against the EIP-1767 schema before field resolution begins; malformed queries must return errors.
Input scalars of type Bytes32 must be 0x-prefixed with exactly 64 hex characters; invalid formats must be rejected.
Input scalars of type Address must be 0x-prefixed with exactly 40 hex characters representing a 20-byte Ethereum address.
Input scalars of type Bytes must have an even number of hex nybbles after the 0x prefix; empty bytes must be represented as 0x.
Input scalars of type BigInt must be valid as either a JSON number or a 0x-prefixed hex string.
The sendRawTransaction mutation must receive a valid RLP-encoded signed transaction; the transaction must be fully decoded and validated before broadcast to the network.
Operations related to signing, compiling, and mining must be denied by the GraphQL API; only query and sendRawTransaction operations are permitted.
Experimental GraphQL fields must use the _client_ naming prefix (e.g., _geth_, _parity_); non-prefixed non-standard fields must be rejected.
The GraphQL endpoint assumes network-level access control is handled externally; operators must implement firewall or reverse proxy protections to prevent unauthorized access and DoS.
After successful transaction broadcast via sendRawTransaction, the response must contain the transaction hash as a Bytes32 value.
A signed message submitted for chain-specific verification must contain an embedded chain ID that can be extracted and compared against the current chain's CHAINID.
The chain ID extracted from a signed message must exactly match the value returned by the CHAINID opcode; any mismatch indicates a cross-chain replay attempt and must cause rejection.
The CHAINID opcode must return the same value as the chain ID used in EIP-155 transaction signing; any inconsistency creates replay attack windows.
The CHAINID opcode must consume exactly G_base gas (2 gas) per execution; it takes no arguments and pushes exactly one 256-bit value onto the stack.
The chain ID configured on the node must match the canonical chain ID for the network; misconfiguration would cause contracts to validate signatures against the wrong chain ID.
During a contentious chain split, previously signed messages with the old chain ID must fail validation on any chain that adopted a new chain ID.

A PoW block received from the network must have its difficulty verified against the expected target, and the cumulative total difficulty must be computed and compared against TERMINAL_TOTAL_DIFFICULTY.
Blocks claiming to reach TTD must be carefully validated; the parent block's total difficulty must be below TTD while the current block pushes it at or above TTD.

Execution payloads received from the beacon chain via Engine API must have deprecated PoW fields validated: difficulty must equal 0, nonce must equal 0x0000000000000000, ommersHash must equal Keccak256(RLP([])), and mixHash must be all zeros.
After the PoW-to-PoS transition is triggered, no further PoW blocks may be accepted as canonical; the consensus mechanism must switch entirely to PoS.
Total difficulty is monotonically non-decreasing across the canonical chain; each block must add non-negative difficulty to the cumulative total.
All execution clients must have identical TERMINAL_TOTAL_DIFFICULTY configuration; divergent TTD values would cause clients to transition at different blocks, resulting in chain splits.
After a fork choice update from the beacon chain, the canonical head must be set to the specified block, and blocks finalized by the beacon chain must be marked as irreversible.
After finalization, competing fork branches must be pruned; blocks not part of the finalized chain should be removed from storage.
After the merge transition, block rewards are eliminated; only transaction priority fees may be credited to the block proposer.
After any deprecated PoW field fails validation in a post-merge block, the block must be immediately rejected without processing transactions.
After the first PoS block is finalized, NewBlock and NewBlockHashes gossip messages must be deprecated; the execution layer must ignore these messages from peers.
A builder bid broadcast on the execution_payload_bid gossip topic must have a valid BLS signature verified against the builder's registered builder_index.
A builder must have sufficient excess balance to cover the bid value for all pending commitments before the bid can be accepted.
For gossip-broadcast bids, the execution_payment field must equal zero; non-zero execution_payment in gossip bids must be rejected.
The bid's parent_block_hash and parent_block_root must reference valid chain state; the slot must be current or next slot.
An execution payload envelope broadcast on the execution_payload gossip topic must have a matching block_hash to the previously accepted bid, and the builder signature must be verified.
After a bid is accepted by the proposer, the builder must pay the bid value to the proposer unconditionally, whether or not the payload is delivered.
After envelope assembly, the state_root in the envelope must equal hash_tree_root(state) computed from running process_execution_payload on a state copy.
Builder withdrawal credentials must have BUILDER_WITHDRAWAL_PREFIX (0x03) as the first byte; any other prefix must be rejected during builder registration.
A builder may legitimately withhold payload delivery if the accepted bid's block is detected as non-canonical; this is not a protocol violation.
An attacker must not be able to forge a builder's BLS signature to submit fraudulent bids; forged bids would drain the builder's balance through forced payment obligations.
For blocks at or after FORK_BLOCK_NUMBER, the difficulty calculation must use the fake block number max(0, block.number - 10,700,000) instead of the actual block number.
After difficulty calculation, the block's stated difficulty must exactly match the computed expected difficulty; any mismatch results in block rejection.
The fork activation is a one-way state transition: once the network passes FORK_BLOCK_NUMBER, the difficulty bomb delay offset applies to all subsequent blocks permanently.
All clients must upgrade before the fork block number is reached; non-upgraded clients will compute different difficulty values, causing a chain split.
The fake_block_number computation must use max(0, ...) to prevent underflow when block.number is less than the offset value.
A Clique block received from a peer must have the ECDSA signature recovered from the extraData suffix (last 65 bytes) and the signer verified against the current authorized signer set.
An authorized signer must not have signed more than 1 of the last floor(N/2)+1 blocks; blocks violating this signing frequency limit must be rejected.
A Clique block's timestamp must be at least parent_timestamp + BLOCK_PERIOD; blocks with earlier timestamps must be rejected.

Clique block extraData must contain a 32-byte vanity prefix and 65-byte signature seal suffix; checkpoint epoch blocks must additionally embed the sorted authorized signer list, nonce=0, and beneficiary=0.
Signer set changes require a majority vote (>= floor(N/2)+1); a minority of signers must never be able to modify the authorized signer set.
After a signer is added or removed via majority vote, all pending votes for that beneficiary must be discarded to prevent stale votes from affecting future tallies.
The signing limit (1 block per floor(N/2)+1 consecutive blocks) prevents any single signer from block spam, even if compromised.
All votes older than one epoch must be discarded at epoch boundaries to prevent unbounded vote accumulation.
In-turn signers set difficulty=2 (INTURN) and out-of-turn signers set difficulty=1 (NOTURN); the fork choice rule prefers higher cumulative difficulty to select the in-turn chain.
Honest signers can vote to deauthorize a compromised signer; the signer set is not immutable and provides a recovery mechanism for key compromise.
The signer set must never become empty; voting rules must prevent removal of the last authorized signer.
After a vote is recorded in a validated block, the tally must be updated and the majority threshold checked immediately; if threshold is met, the signer set change must be applied atomically.
A contract deployment transaction submitted by an external deployer must have its init code executed in a gas-bounded environment; the resulting runtime bytecode must be validated before storage.
After init code execution, the first byte of the returned runtime bytecode must be checked; if it equals 0xEF, the deployment must trigger an exceptional abort consuming all remaining gas.
After successful first-byte validation (byte != 0xEF), the runtime bytecode must be stored at the new contract address in the account trie.
The 0xEF first-byte check must apply uniformly to all contract creation paths: external transactions, CREATE opcode, and CREATE2 opcode. No deployment path may bypass this validation.
Empty bytecode (zero-length) returned from init code is allowed since it has no first byte to check; empty contracts remain valid and deployable.
Existing contracts deployed before the fork activation that start with 0xEF are legitimate legacy code and must not be affected by the new validation rule.
After a CREATE opcode exceptional abort due to 0xEF, the parent contract's stack must have 0 pushed (failure), and all gas provided to the CREATE call must be consumed.
After a successful CREATE opcode (first byte != 0xEF), the child contract code must be stored and the child contract address pushed onto the parent's stack.
After a CREATE2 exceptional abort due to 0xEF, 0 must be pushed to stack and gas consumed; the deterministic address must remain unused.
After a successful CREATE2 (first byte != 0xEF), the contract code must be stored at the pre-computed deterministic address and that address pushed onto the stack.
The bytecode validation (first byte check against 0xEF) is a simple equality comparison: byte == 0xEF triggers rejection, any other value (0x00-0xEE, 0xF0-0xFF) passes.
